ai.description: Thampi's Torrent Frog is a small, slender species (25–30 mm) with a brown dorsum and mottled flanks. It is distinguished by a pointed snout and elongated, slender digits with distinct toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus thampii* is best distinguished by its unique, vivid reddish-brown to orange coloration on the dorsal surface, which contrasts sharply with the darker, mottled flanks.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus thampii* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests of the southern Western Ghats, typically found near fast-flowing, rocky streams above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: Thampi's Torrent Frog is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates along fast-flowing forest streams during the daylight hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus thampii* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in subterranean nests beneath stream-bed gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: Micrixalus thampii is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Micrixalus thampii* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted while the frog perches near fast-flowing forest streams.
